subject.title: Feature: Inter-session progress streaming for sessions_send (ACP/long-running session support)

question: Should OpenClaw expose caller-visible run progress for peer `sessions_send` runs, and should the canonical surface be `sessions_subscribe`, `agent.events`, or an explicit `sessions_send` progress mode?
rationale: The unresolved work defines a cross-session event observation boundary that could expose intermediate run state, so automation should not choose the API, authorization, redaction, retention, replay, or channel delivery semantics alone.

options.title: Design a bounded event-read contract
options.body: Approve an additive run-event observation API with explicit session authorization, redaction, retention, replay, and tests before implementing the tool surface.

options.title: Limit this to final delivery semantics
options.body: Keep the current accepted-plus-final-announce model and document that peer progress visibility remains out of scope for now.

options.title: Defer to broader process events
options.body: Let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/52826 define the canonical process/step event model first, then map sessions_send progress onto it later.

recommendation.title: Design a bounded event-read contract
recommendation.body: Approve an additive run-event observation API with explicit session authorization, redaction, retention, replay, and tests before implementing the tool surface.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history across sessions_send, A2A delivery, agent.wait, and structured agent-event surfaces.
